points.quote: Headless plugins use a single shared backend host and have no frontend. (VS Code extensions and Theia plugins are named, but nothing on runtime install/removal versus built-in Theia extensions)

For each connected frontend, the Theia backend forks a Node child process ... Plugins can also run in a browser web worker ... The Ext side runs in the plugin host. It can't use Theia services directly.

The API is declared in `packages/plugin/src/theia.d.ts`. `createAPIFactory` in `packages/plugin-ext/src/plugin/plugin-context.ts` builds one API object per plugin. ... VS Code extensions use `vscode`, handled in `packages/plugin-ext-vscode/src/node/plugin-vscode-init.ts:60`. It starts from the Theia API and overrides a few members.

In Node hosts, module loading is overridden by replacing `module._load`: Theia plugins use `@theia/plugin` ... VS Code extensions use `vscode` ... In web workers, the API is assigned to `window['theia']`.

Each feature has a matching pair of interfaces, such as `LanguagesExt` and `LanguagesMain`, defined in `plugin-ext/src/common/plugin-api-rpc.ts`. Only methods starting with `$` are callable over RPC. ... Each side holds a proxy of the other side's interface.
For each connected frontend, the Theia backend forks a Node child process ... The browser reaches the host through the Theia backend, which only relays messages in both directions.
The transport is an `RpcProtocol` using msgpackr encoding. ... Objects with functions can't be serialised. The creating side caches the object and sends a handle (an id).
Headless plugins use a single shared backend host and have no frontend. ... For headless plugins, Main runs in Node instead. (purpose of application-specific extension points not stated)
